text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended lower in a correction to recent sharp gains. Most active May tumbled $30 to close at $1.533 per tonne, while March gave up $18 to close at $1,535 per tonne. Traders said prices have to fall further to attract fresh industry involvement. Robusta producers have called off a meeting in Bali (Indonesia) due on Thursday after an Ivorian Minister failed to make the trip. The producers met informally but no decision was made on the sharing of export quotas agreed recently at an ACPC meeting in Brazil. In New York arabica futures closed sharply lower on profit taking. AFRICA - African robusta producers will undertake export cuts outlined by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) Donald Kaberuka, chief economist at the Inter-African Coffee Organization (IACO), told Reuters. He declined to reveal the allocations for each of the African countries, saying it was an internal matter. The ACPC decided at a meeting in Brazil on January 23 to reduce members' exports by 1.3 million bags (1 million bags robustas and 0.3 million bags arabicas), in addition to an existing export ceiling of 26.28 million bags between January and June 1997. UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell to 20,795 bags on February 4, from 21,051 bags. While stocks in New York, San Francisco and Miami remained unchanged, stocks in New Orleans fell by 256 bags to 4,501 bags (4,757 bags).
